label: override_express
point: Reversed Lin's 924(c) convictions because the jury instruction on 'use' was foreclosed by Bailey's active-employment reading.
change: Added a separate offense for possessing a firearm 'in furtherance of' a crime of violence or drug crime, and restructured penalties into graded minimums.
why: The 1998 Act answered Bailey by reaching possession in furtherance, closing the gap that forced reversal in Lin; the committee report cites Lin as an example of convictions lost under Bailey.

label: unrelated
point: Treated a motion invoking Rule 60(b)(5) and 3582(c) as a successive 2255 motion because it attacked the underlying sentence.
change: Let defendants themselves move for compassionate release after exhausting BOP remedies or 30 days.
why: The change concerns who may file a compassionate-release motion, not whether a sentence attack is properly characterized as a 2255 motion.

label: unrelated
point: Denied summary judgment on written-description invalidity under 112 because expert reports raised fact issues.
change: Renumbered 112 into lettered subsections and changed 'inventor' wording to include joint inventors.
why: The written-description requirement the court applied was not changed in substance.

label: unrelated
point: Addressed whether a debtor's attorney's unpaid fees from a prior chapter 13 case are disallowed as unreasonable under 502(b)(4).
change: Added a timeliness rule for governmental tax claims on returns filed under section 1308 in chapter 13.
why: The tax-claim timing provision has nothing to do with attorney-fee reasonableness under 502(b)(4).

label: unrelated
point: Applied the 112 para. 6 means-plus-function equivalency analysis to the 'way' prong.
change: Renumbered 112 into lettered subsections (para. 6 became 112(f)) with wording changes on inventors.
why: Renumbering left the means-plus-function rule unchanged.

label: unrelated
point: Held a prepetition security interest in assigned insurance commissions extends to postpetition commissions under 552(b)(1).
change: Changed 'product' to 'products' in 552(b).
why: A one-word grammatical change does not affect the holding.

label: override_express
point: Held that the FCA conspiracy provision, 3729(a)(3), reaches only conspiracies to get a false claim paid and not conspiracies to commit reverse false claims under (a)(7).
change: FERA rewrote the conspiracy provision to cover conspiracies to violate any of subparagraphs (A), (B), (D), (E), (F) or (G), including reverse false claims.
why: The new words would make the conspiracy claim viable, and the committee report cites this decision as the holding being corrected.

label: unrelated
point: Construed a supervised-release condition to 'participate' in sex-offender treatment; 2252 was cited only for the underlying conviction background.
change: Raised the maximum penalty for possession offenses involving prepubescent minors.
why: The penalty change has nothing to do with the supervised-release question decided.

label: unrelated
point: Contrasted the ADA's definition of qualified individual, which has no present-ability temporal requirement, with the NJLAD's in holding leave was not a reasonable accommodation under state law.
change: Struck 'with a disability' from the term 'qualified individual with a disability.'
why: The conforming change does not alter the 'with or without reasonable accommodation' language the court relied on.

label: override_implicit
point: Held that 'facility in interstate or foreign commerce' in 1958(a) requires actual interstate or foreign use of the facility in the particular instance, not the broad 'facility of interstate commerce' definition, though the conviction stood on international calls.
change: Changed 1958(a) to 'facility of interstate or foreign commerce' and conformed the definition, so intrastate use of such a facility suffices.
why: The amendment adopts the broad reading the court rejected, so its narrow interpretation no longer holds; nothing in the packet ties Congress to this case.

label: unrelated
point: Denied reconsideration of the denial of acquittal on a 2252 child-pornography count; 2423(b) was cited only as the charge on another count.
change: Rewrote 2423(b) to cover travel for 'illicit sexual conduct', dropped conspiracy language, and raised the maximum to 30 years.
why: The 2423(b) changes do not touch the 2252 issue decided; the committee report cites the earlier Sims opinion in this case on the virtual-pornography defense, not on 2423(b).

label: unrelated
point: Cited 405 for the rule that new evidence warrants remand only if material and good cause exists, and found the post-hearing MRI not material.
change: Added advance designation of representative payees and payee oversight provisions to 405(j).
why: The representative-payee amendments are unrelated to sentence-six remand standards.

label: related
point: The Fifth Circuit held ERISA, including the anti-alienation provision of 1056(d)(1), did not preempt Louisiana community-property claims by a predeceased spouse's heirs to plan benefits.
change: Added an exception to the anti-alienation rule permitting offsets of benefits for amounts owed to the plan for fiduciary violations or crimes against the plan.
why: Same anti-alienation provision but a different point, and the conference report expressly says it does not modify the Supreme Court's result in Boggs.

label: unrelated
point: Applied the guideline enhancement for a firearm described in 921(a)(30) and attributed a codefendant's machine gun to the defendant as relevant conduct.
change: Redefined 'antique firearm' in 921(a)(16) and added a definition of 'secure gun storage or safety device.'
why: The changes are to different paragraphs of 921(a) than the one the guideline referenced.

label: related
point: Held divorce-decree obligations (including attorney's fees) were support under 523(a)(5) and thus nondischargeable despite the creditor's failure to object, rather than property settlements under 523(a)(15).
change: BAPCPA rewrote 523(a), including recasting (a)(5) as domestic support obligations and making (a)(15) property-settlement debts nondischargeable without the prior adversary-proceeding requirement, plus tax and luxury-goods changes.
why: The amendments reduce the importance of the support/property distinction but would not change the result that these support debts are nondischargeable.

label: unrelated
point: Held a roommate who regularly used the called line had statutory standing under the TCPA even though he was not the intended 'called party.'
change: Exempted calls made to collect debts owed to or guaranteed by the United States and allowed FCC limits on such calls.
why: The federal-debt exemption does not bear on who may sue as the called party.

label: override_implicit
point: Affirmed denial of a preliminary injunction on the federal dilution claim because Vuitton showed no actual dilution under the 1127 definition as read in Moseley.
change: The TDRA struck the 1127 definition of dilution and replaced it with a likelihood-of-dilution standard for blurring and tarnishment.
why: Under the new words actual dilution is no longer required, so the ground on which the dilution claim failed is gone; Congress was responding to Moseley, not this decision.

label: codifies
point: The en banc court held that a contractual duty to account for or return excess government property is an existing 'obligation' supporting a reverse false claim under 3729(a)(7).
change: FERA rewrote the reverse-false-claims provision and defined 'obligation' as an established duty, whether or not fixed, arising from contract, regulation, and other sources.
why: The new definition writes in the contract-based obligation Pemco recognized, and the committee report cites Pemco in its discussion of the provision.

label: override_express
point: Following Totten, held FCA 3729(a)(1) and conspiracy liability require presentment of a claim to a federal officer or employee, so claims submitted to the state Medicaid agency were not actionable.
change: FERA removed the 'to an officer or employee of the United States Government' presentment language and made liability turn on false claims, including requests to grantees.
why: The amendment eliminates the presentment requirement the court relied on, and the committee report cites this decision as an example of the Totten line it corrects.

label: unrelated
point: Held the Child Welfare Act foster-care maintenance provisions create no privately enforceable rights, distinguishing Wilder's reading of the Medicaid Act 1396a(a)(13).
change: Extended the Medicare cost-sharing (QI) period end date from December 2013 to March 2014.
why: A date extension in an unrelated paragraph has nothing to do with the decision.

label: codifies
point: Held that punitive damages received in a physical-injury (wrongful death) case are not excludable from gross income under 104(a)(2).
change: The 1996 Act limited 104(a)(2) to damages 'other than punitive damages' on account of personal physical injuries, and denied physical-injury treatment to emotional distress.
why: Congress made punitive damages taxable going forward, agreeing with the Tenth Circuit's result; the report notes this case's pending Supreme Court review.

label: override_implicit
point: Held Dunaway was not 'regarded as' disabled because he lacked evidence Ford believed his knee condition substantially limited a major life activity, applying Sutton and Toyota.
change: Changed 12112(a) to bar discrimination 'on the basis of disability' and, in the same Act, redefined 'regarded as' so it no longer requires a perceived substantial limitation.
why: Under the ADAAA a perceived impairment suffices for a regarded-as claim, so the decision's reasoning no longer works; the Act rejected Sutton and Toyota, not this decision by name.

label: codifies
point: Held that in a claim to reopen VA must give notice of the elements of the claim found insufficient in the prior denial and of what new and material evidence would substantiate them.
change: Required VA to prescribe regulations specifying notice contents by claim type, including claims to reopen.
why: The committee report cites Kent approvingly and directs that reopening notices reference the prior decision's deficient element, consistent with the holding.
